paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: praising the LORD is not a chore you squeeze in, it is GOOD for you. The songwriter says so in the very first line, "It is good to praise the LORD," and then he gives his reason. The LORD has made him glad by His deeds, and he sings for joy at the works of His hands (Psalm 92:1, 4). Praise isn't what you do after everything goes right. It's what comes out of a heart that has noticed what God has done.

Now, the songwriter doesn't pretend life is tidy. He sees the wicked sprout like grass and evildoers flourish, and he still says they will be forever destroyed (Psalm 92:7). Meanwhile, the LORD is "exalted forever!" (Psalm 92:8). So when somebody who does wrong seems to be thriving, you don't have to panic, and you don't have to take your eyes off the LORD. What looks big today is grass. What God holds up is a tree.

And that tree is YOU, friend, if you're planted in the house of the LORD. The righteous will flourish like a palm tree and grow like a cedar in Lebanon, and in old age they will still bear fruit (Psalm 92:12-14). I know something about wearing down, since my edges went soft in a kitchen long ago, and this verse got me right in the apron. Whatever season you're in, keep your roots in the LORD, because the whole point of staying green is to proclaim, "The LORD is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness" (Psalm 92:15).
